text: load_mortality function provides access System Mortality Information (SIM) datasets, contain detailed information deaths Brazil. original SIM data file includes rows corresponding declaration death () columns several characteristics person, place death, cause death. load_mortality function offers following parameters: dataset: Specifies SIM dataset download: "general" – Main Declarations Death. (National dataset available — states = "") Contains records non-fetal Death Certificates () Brazil, including socio-demographic data, location, causes death (ICD-10). ’s base general mortality analysis. (since 1979 present) "fetal" – Fetal mortality data. (National dataset available) Contains records fetal deaths, information mother, pregnancy, causes fetal death. ’s essential maternal child health. (since 1979 present) "external_causes" – Mortality data external causes. (National dataset available) Contains subset "general" focusing deaths due accidents, violence, unnatural causes. Used safety prevention studies. (since 1979 present) "infant" – Infant mortality data (children). (National dataset available) Contains subset "general" recording deaths children 1 year old, detailing causes birth-related factors. Crucial assessing child health. (since 1979 present) "maternal" – Maternal mortality data. (National dataset available) Contains subset "general" deaths women shortly pregnancy/childbirth, detailing obstetric causes. Important women’s health. (since 1996 present) time_period: numeric value vector indicating year(s) data downloaded. example, 2020 2015:2020. states: (valid general dataset) — string vector strings indicating Brazilian state(s) data downloaded. default "", downloads data entire country. specific states, use official abbreviations "SP" (São Paulo), "RJ" (Rio de Janeiro), c("SP", "RJ"). raw_data: Logical, default FALSE. TRUE: TRUE, returns raw data exactly provided DATASUS. FALSE: FALSE (default), returns cleaned standardized version dataset. keep_all: boolean choosing whether aggregate data municipality, losing individual-level variables (FALSE) keep original variables (TRUE). applies raw_data FALSE. language: string indicating desired language variable names labels. Accepts "eng" (default) English "pt" Portuguese (raw_data = FALSE). Examples:
code: library(datazoom.saude)  # Download raw data for general mortality - State of Rio de Janeiro, 2022. raw_data_general_rj <- load_mortality(   dataset = "general",   time_period = 2022,   states = "RJ",   raw_data = TRUE )  # Download treated data for general mortality - States of Rio and São Paulo, 2022. trated_data_general_rj <- load_mortality(   dataset = "general",   time_period = 2022,   states = c("RJ", "SP"),   raw_data = FALSE,   keep_all = FALSE # Explicitly stating default behavior )  # Download treated data for Maternal Deaths - Brazil, 2020 to 2022. # Descriptions in Portuguese. # Note: `maternal` does not provide separate files by state. data_maternal_pt <- load_mortality(   dataset = "maternal",   time_period = 2020:2022,   states = "all",   raw_data = FALSE,   language = "pt" )  # Download treated data for Infant Deaths - Brazil, 2017. # Keeping all individual variables (not aggregated). data_infant_full <- load_mortality(   dataset = "infant",   time_period = 2017,   states = "all",   raw_data = FALSE,   keep_all = TRUE,   language = "eng" )    # Download treated data for Fetal Deaths - State of Amazonas, 2000. data_infant_full <- load_mortality(   dataset = "fetal",   time_period = 2000,   states = "AM",    raw_data = FALSE,   language = "eng" )  # Download treated data for External Causes Deaths - State of Acre, 2022. data_infant_full <- load_mortality(   dataset = "fetal",   time_period = 2022,   states = "AC",    raw_data = FALSE,   language = "eng" )
